title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Specialty appliance and machine cleaning
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: "I will clean your oven" is a service. "I will clean the oven interior, racks and glass to the checklist on your booking sheet, show you the result with photos before I leave, and return within the agreed days to fix any checklist item I have missed, at no charge" is an offer. The customer buys a clean appliance and the certainty that a missed item will be put right. It does not include any repair of the appliance's function.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Set a clear outcome, such as a named clean on a named appliance; a time frame, such as the visit window; the work the customer must do, such as clearing the area and removing loose items; the certainty you give, such as a checklist and before-and-after photos (after the privacy steps in the safety section); and the risk you carry. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Show the minimum on the offer
instruction.body: Appliance cleaning often has an item price and a minimum charge. A Sydney price list shows a single 60 cm oven at $199 for a non-member, with a minimum for the service of $204 (Fantastic Cleaners, updated 15 July 2026). The minimum can override the item price on a small job, so state it on the offer next to the item price. The same list has a membership tier that lowers item and minimum prices. That is one vendor's repeat-client mechanism, not market evidence, so do not copy it without testing your own numbers.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction and setting exclusions
instruction.body: Make the booking, the access and the handover simple. Name what you do not do: this offer does not include opening or adjusting gas or electrical components, and it does not include repairing an appliance's function. Victoria's gas guidance says only the right gasfitting endorsement holder may work on certain gas appliances (Energy Safe Victoria, reviewed 5 June 2024). Keep those items on the exclusions list so the customer knows where the cleaning stops.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: The Australian Consumer Law consumer guarantees apply to services. They require due care and skill, delivery within a reasonable time where none is agreed, and fitness for any stated purpose, and a business cannot remove them by contract or notice (ACCC, last modified 17 July 2026). A written fix-first step for a missed item is a useful promise. Consumer Victoria describes a fix-first step for services not done with due care and skill, but it does not set a fix-window length, so write your own window (Consumer Victoria, 13 October 2023). Do not promise a cleaning result, such as a stain-free oven, that you cannot show.

instruction.heading: Price the offer as one total
instruction.body: Show one total price for the visit, including any unavoidable fee, and say whether GST is included. The ACCC's price display guidance (2 October 2026) says the total must include unavoidable fees, and that card surcharges cannot be charged from 1 October 2026. Check any membership or minimum rule against that guidance before you publish it.

procedure: Write the cleaning outcome for each appliance type in one sentence a customer would repeat.
Set a visit time frame that you have checked against your own completed jobs, and record how often you meet it.
List what the customer must do, such as clearing the area and removing loose items, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a checklist and before-and-after photos, after checking the privacy steps.
Write the exclusions for gas and electrical components and for repairs, and state the minimum charge beside the item price.
Decide the fix-first window for missed checklist items, and check that you can afford it.

workedExamples.situation: A non-member books a single 60 cm oven clean only. The Sydney price list shows $199 for that item and a minimum for the service of $204 (Fantastic Cleaners, updated 15 July 2026).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the quote say, and what is charged for this job?
workedExamples.reasoning: The minimum applies, so the job is charged at least $204, which is $5 above the item price. The quote shows the item price, the minimum, and that the minimum applies to this job. It shows one total including any unavoidable fee, and states whether GST is included. This is arithmetic from one vendor's published list, so it shows the logic of a minimum, not what the owner must charge.

workedExamples.situation: A member books the same 60 cm oven clean. The list shows a member item price of $159 and a member minimum of $164 (Fantastic Cleaners, updated 15 July 2026). During the visit, the client asks the cleaner to adjust the oven's gas burner flame.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the member's charge, and what should the cleaner say about the burner?
workedExamples.reasoning: The member's charge is at least $164, because the minimum applies. The cleaner does not adjust the burner. Victoria's gas guidance says only a suitable gasfitting endorsement holder may work on certain gas appliances, and the cleaning offer excludes gas components. The cleaner records the request, explains the exclusion and suggests the client ask a suitably licensed gasfitter. Any repair is quoted separately by that licensed person.

equipmentAndPpe: Rate card showing item prices, minimum charge and exclusions
Checklist for each appliance type, with space for photos and the client's sign-off
Written fix-first policy, with the window the owner has set
Safety data sheet for every oven or machine cleaner used on the job (see the safety section)

commonErrors.error: Quoting the item price on a small job where the minimum applies.
commonErrors.prevention: Show the minimum beside the item price, and state that it applies to small jobs.

commonErrors.error: Adjusting, opening or repairing a gas or electrical component because the client asks.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep gas and electrical component work on the exclusions list, and refer the client to the right licensed person.

commonErrors.error: Promising a cleaning result, such as a stain-free oven, that you cannot show.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the result on the checklist, and show it with photos at sign-off.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a membership price suits your business. Gap: no washing machine, dishwasher or fridge price was sourced.
commonErrors.prevention: Test any membership or tier price against your own costs before offering it, and set prices for uncovered appliances from your own figures.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consumer guarantees for services apply under the Australian Consumer Law, and a business cannot exclude them by contract (ACCC, 17 July 2026). Business guidance only: this lesson does not grant any licence or authority.

Victoria only: Energy Safe Victoria says only persons with a Type B gasfitting endorsement may work on Type B appliances, that gasfitters should only do work they are competent to do, and that consumers should ask to see the gasfitter's licence. The page does not cover cleaning. Check the gas and electrical licence rules for NSW, Queensland and Western Australia, which the research did not verify.
Show one total price including unavoidable fees, and state whether it includes GST (ACCC, 2 October 2026).

Oven and machine cleaners are chemicals that may be hazardous. SafeWork SA's safety data sheet guidance says the person running the business must obtain the safety data sheet for hazardous chemicals used at work, make it available to workers, and use it to write a safe procedure. Confirm each product's classification from its safety data sheet, and follow it.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: An appliance cleaning offer promises a checked clean, a visible minimum and a written fix-first window.
Exclude gas and electrical component work, and refer it to the licensed person.
Gap: one Sydney vendor list is the only sourced appliance price. No washing machine, dishwasher or fridge price, and no trade body or referral channel, was verified.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an appliance cleaning offer does the customer buy?
options: A checked clean of the named appliance, with a fix-first window for missed items

knowledgeChecks.question: A non-member books a 60 cm oven clean. The item price is $199 and the minimum is $204. What should the quote show?
options: The item price only, since the client will not notice the minimum
The item price and the minimum, and that the minimum applies to this small job
A price of $199 with the minimum hidden in the terms
No price, until the cleaner has seen the oven

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks you to adjust a gas burner during an oven clean. What does Victoria's gas guidance say about who may do this work?
options: Any cleaner who has used the oven before
Only persons with the right gasfitting endorsement, such as Type B for Type B appliances
The client, with the cleaner watching
Nobody, so the appliance must be sold
